skill.name: ffind
skill.description: Guides firmware and IoT security analysis with ffind, including file type detection, output selection, and controlled filesystem extraction.
skill.summary: Analyze firmware files with ffind and extract embedded filesystems when approved.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate firmware analysis purpose, but it instructs agents to run ffind and several sudo extraction commands. Markdown-only option and fence detections were dismissed as false positives, while external command, sudo, and temporary directory risks were confirmed. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before any sudo command and explain why elevated privileges are needed for the selected image.
Resolve the intended iothackbot ffind binary before use and avoid running commands against paths the user has not confirmed.
Prefer a user-approved, access-controlled output directory and remove extracted files when analysis is complete.

content.value_statement: Firmware images often hide filesystems and security artifacts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ffind scans, type summaries, and controlled extraction.
actual_capabilities: Guide ffind scans for one or more local file paths.
Help identify artifact file types and optionally show all file types.
Explain text, JSON, and quiet output modes for ffind results.
Guide ext2, ext3, ext4, and F2FS extraction when dependencies are installed.
Help choose an extraction directory and verify the intended ffind binary.
limitations: Requires the iothackbot ffind tool and supporting filesystem utilities to be installed.
Extraction may require sudo and must not run without user approval.
Results depend on local file access, permissions, and the installed tool version.
Does not replace malware sandboxing, forensic validation, or manual review.

use_cases.title: Inspect Firmware Images
use_cases.description: Find embedded filesystems and artifact file types before deeper reverse engineering.

use_cases.title: Validate Device Builds
use_cases.description: Check generated firmware packages for expected filesystem content and unexpected file types.

use_cases.title: Triage Unknown Binaries
use_cases.description: Summarize file types across collected images and decide whether extraction is justified.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a single firmware image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ffind to analyze the firmware file at [path]. Summarize detected artifact types and ask before any extraction.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison across two or more images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these paths with ffind: [paths]. Compare the file type summaries and call out unusual artifact types.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled Extraction
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced extraction planning before elevated commands.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [path] with ffind and propose an extraction plan. Include the output directory, required privileges, and approval checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Tool Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced environment check when another ffind binary may exist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether the installed ffind is the iothackbot version before analyzing [path]. Use a full path if the system binary is different.

output: The extraction plan uses a user-approved directory with restricted access.

best_practices: Confirm target paths and authorization before running any scan.
Verify the intended iothackbot ffind binary when another ffind may be installed.
Use controlled extraction directories and review permissions after extraction.
anti_patterns: Running sudo extraction without explicit user approval.
Extracting untrusted firmware into shared temporary directories without cleanup.
Assuming a system ffind binary supports the iothackbot command options.

faq.question: What does this skill help analyze?
faq.answer: It helps use ffind to inspect firmware files, identify file types, and plan filesystem extraction.

faq.question: Does it run extraction automatically?
faq.answer: No. Extraction should only run after the user approves the target path, output directory, and privilege requirement.

faq.question: Which filesystems are covered?
faq.answer: The skill describes ext2, ext3, ext4, and F2FS extraction when required system tools are available.

faq.question: Why is sudo mentioned?
faq.answer: Some extraction workflows need root privileges. This creates security risk and should require clear user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it produce machine-readable output?
faq.answer: Yes. The ffind tool supports a JSON output mode when the installed version includes that option.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm the target file, verify the correct ffind binary, and choose a restricted output directory.
